notes: Prevents file descriptor, socket, or lock leaks

rule: Formal deviation records with safety justifications must be logged for every waived rule

project: MISRA C (public guidance and enforcement tooling)
rule: Code must strictly conform to specified ISO C standard version without non-standard extensions
notes: Compiler extensions must be disabled or isolated in hardware abstraction layers

rule: ARR30-C: Do not form or use out-of-bounds pointers or array subscripts
notes: Prevents buffer overflows and arbitrary memory corruption

rule: DCL30-C: Declare objects with appropriate storage durations; never return pointers to automatic local objects
notes: Prevents dangling stack pointer access after function returns

rule: ENV33-C: Do not call system() because it can result in command injection vulnerabilities
notes: Enforces use of execve or POSIX spawn with explicit arguments

rule: ERR33-C: Detect and handle standard library errors from functions returning error codes
notes: Ensures error status of POSIX and C library calls are validated

rule: EXP34-C: Do not dereference null pointers; validate pointer before use
notes: Eliminates null pointer dereference crashes and exploitable traps

rule: FIO30-C: Exclude user input from format strings in printf-family functions
notes: Prevents format string vulnerabilities that allow memory read/write

rule: INT30-C: Ensure that unsigned integer operations do not wrap in security-critical calculations
notes: Prevents integer wrapping leading to undersized buffer allocations

rule: INT31-C: Ensure that integer conversions do not result in lost or misinterpreted data
notes: Catches truncation and signed/unsigned sign bugs

rule: INT32-C: Ensure that operations on signed integers do not result in undefined overflow
notes: Signed integer overflow is undefined behavior in C

rule: MEM30-C: Do not access freed memory (use-after-free prevention)
notes: Enforced statically and dynamically via AddressSanitizer

rule: MEM31-C: Free dynamically allocated memory when no longer needed to prevent resource exhaustion
notes: Prevents memory exhaustion Denial-of-Service

rule: STR31-C: Guarantee that storage for strings has sufficient space for character data and null terminator
notes: Prevents off-by-one buffer overflows in string manipulation

project: NASA JPL Power of Ten / JPL C standard
rule: Rule 2: All loops must have a fixed, statically determinable upper bound
notes: Prevents runaway execution and ensures worst-case execution time (WCET)

project: NASA JPL Power of Ten / JPL C standard
rule: Rule 3: Do not use dynamic memory allocation after task initialization
notes: Eliminates out-of-memory errors and heap fragmentation during flight

project: NASA JPL Power of Ten / JPL C standard
rule: Rule 4: Function length bounded to what fits on a single printed page (~60 lines LOC)

project: NASA JPL Power of Ten / JPL C standard

mechanical_form: static AST assertion count per function
notes: Assertions must validate preconditions, postconditions, and loop invariants

project: NASA JPL Power of Ten / JPL C standard
rule: Rule 6: Declare data objects at the smallest possible scope
notes: Hides state and avoids accidental cross-module data dependencies

project: NASA JPL Power of Ten / JPL C standard
rule: Rule 7: Check return value of every non-void function and validate parameter values
notes: Never ignore error returns; cast explicitly to void only when safe

project: NASA JPL Power of Ten / JPL C standard
rule: Rule 8: Preprocessor use must be limited to file inclusion and simple conditional compilation
notes: Macros must not redefine syntax or hide control flow

project: NASA JPL Power of Ten / JPL C standard
rule: Rule 9: Restrict pointer use: at most one level of dereferencing; no function pointers
notes: Makes pointer aliasing statically analyzable and prevents function pointer corruption

project: NASA JPL Power of Ten / JPL C standard
rule: Rule 10: Compile code daily with all compiler warnings enabled (-Wall -Wextra -Werror) and zero warnings
notes: Code must compile cleanly under at least two distinct compilers

rule: Rule A0-1-1: A project shall not contain instances of non-volatile variables being accessed concurrently
notes: Prevents data races in multi-threaded ECU applications

rule: Rule A0-1-2: The value returned by a function having a non-void return type shall be used
notes: Guarantees error returns and computations are not ignored

rule: Rule A0-1-3: Every function shall be called at least once (no dead functions)
notes: Eliminates dead code to reduce complexity and attack surface

rule: Rule A5-0-1: The condition of an if-statement or iteration-statement shall have type bool
notes: Prohibits implicit conversions of pointers and integers in conditions

rule: Rule A5-1-1: Literal values shall not be used apart from type initialization, 0, and 1
notes: Mandates named constants for magic numbers

rule: Rule A6-5-1: A for-loop counter shall not have floating-point type
notes: Prevents non-deterministic loop iteration counts caused by float rounding

rule: Rule A7-1-1: Constexpr or const shall be declared for variables not modified after initialization
notes: Improves immutability guarantees and compiler optimization

rule: Rule A8-4-7: In-parameters for cheap-to-copy types shall be passed by value rather than reference
notes: Optimizes ABI register passing for fundamental types

rule: Rule A15-0-1: A function shall not exit with an unhandled exception
notes: Functions marked noexcept and main must not allow exceptions to escape

rule: Rule A18-5-2: Non-placement new and delete expressions shall not be used
notes: Enforces smart pointers or custom memory allocators

rule: Deviations from required AUTOSAR rules must be documented in formal safety cases

rule: Code must strictly conform to the approved AUTOSAR C++14 language feature subset

rule: Header guards must format as <PROJECT>_<PATH>_<FILE>_H_

rule: Include order must follow: related header, C system, C++ standard, other libraries, project headers
notes: Standardizes include dependencies and minimizes hidden header assumptions

rule: All C++ code must reside in a namespace; using-directives in headers or global scope are prohibited
notes: Prevents symbol clashes in massive codebases

rule: Single-argument constructors must be explicitly marked explicit
notes: Prevents unintended implicit conversions during call dispatch

rule: Exclusive pointer ownership must be expressed via std::unique_ptr, not raw pointers
notes: Raw pointers must only be used as non-owning borrow references

rule: C++ source files must format according to Google C++ Style via clang-format

rule: In Python, import packages and modules only; do not import individual classes or functions (except typing)

rule: Public Python functions and methods must have PEP 484 type annotations

rule: Python lines must not exceed 80 characters (or 100 with Black/Pyink auto-formatter)

rule: Wildcard imports (from module import *) are strictly prohibited in Python
notes: Prevents unexpected symbol namespace pollution

rule: C++ exceptions are prohibited in traditional Google codebases; error status types must be used

rule: Source code must pass cpplint.py static style checker without warnings

rule: Contributors must sign Google Contributor License Agreement before code acceptance

rule: C++ code must conform to Google C++ Style Guide formatted via clang-format

notes: Clients must build from source at head rather than link dynamic libraries

rule: Symbols in namespace absl::internal or internal/ directories must not be used externally

rule: Code must support compilers released within the last 5 years per platform policy

rule: Abseil must maintain working CMake build configurations alongside Bazel

rule: New APIs must demonstrate widespread existing usage before consideration for Abseil
